precepts.text: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves. That striving spirit will unravel things, and people can see it when you move like that. Some security brothers, be careful: you get ahead of yourself ordering people around. That is your brother and your sister; deal with somebody like you want to be dealt with. No member is better than the next; we are all working toward the same goal, the kingdom. If we have this mind frame, we are going to move mountains.
precepts.point: Nobody should be bogging down your talents and gifts; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching others those talents where possible.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
One body, many members, so “Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.”

That striving spirit will unravel things, and people can see it when you move like that. Some of you security brothers, be careful. Because you're able to say move over here, move over there, you get ahead of yourself playing musical chairs: get up, go over here, no, sit right here, don't say nothing, hop on one leg, Simon says shut up. That's your brother; that's your sister. Deal with somebody the way you want to be dealt with.

Yes, some folks are hard-headed and act a straight fool, and sometimes you have to speak a certain way to let them know you're serious, because some don't understand organization. But no member is better than the next. We are all the same, working toward the same goal: we want the kingdom.

If we have this mind frame, esteeming each other better than ourselves, we are going to move mountains. That is what it means that the many members are yet but one body.

precepts.text: Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. How can I apply this gift to help somebody else, to benefit my people, to benefit the school? Some brothers had the gift of reaching people on the flyers: they can get a flyer into the hand of a man that just refused everybody else. You might have used that gift to hustle in the world, but that is not why you were given it. When your mind has been renewed you understand: God gave me that gift so I can get the word out. If you are not using the gift for the Lord, the Lord did not give it to you. God gives these gifts with purpose.
precepts.point: All these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will. God has divided to every man as he wanted. Everyone has received something. New brothers and sisters, you are trying to discover what the Lord wants you to do here, because you woke up in this time period for a reason. What are you bringing to the table? How are you going to benefit your people and carry this truth to the next level? Sisters, the same: this is not just about the brothers, it is about a nation.

note.label: Members of the Body  Pt2

precepts.why:
When you have these gifts, what do you do with them? Paul: “Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.” How can I apply this gift to help somebody? How can I use what I know to help somebody else, to benefit my people, to benefit the school? What little brick can I put in that is going to bring us to where we need to be? That is the mind frame we must have when we function as a body.

Take the gift of reaching people. Some brothers can get a flyer into anybody's hand, even people who do not want one. The man walks off from one brother and tells him to go screw himself, and then another brother walks up the same way and the man leaves with a flyer in his hand saying, all right brothers, y'all take care. People have different gifts.

You might have used that gift in the world to hustle and get over on people, but that is not why you were given it. When you come into this truth and your mind is renewed, you understand: God gave me that gift so I can get the word out, relate to people, and show them thus saith the Lord.

If you are not using that gift for the Lord, the Lord did not give it to you; Satan gave it to you. God gives these gifts with purpose, “to profit withal”: every man looking on the things of others.

precepts.text: Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
precepts.point: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. Looking means acting when a brother struggles.

note.label: The Highway of the Upright: an Israelites's Strait Journey

precepts.why:
“Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.” If I esteem you better than myself, then within my power I have to help you come up with a solution, or help provide it. “Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.” That does not mean just looking: yeah, he's struggling like hell. No. Look means action. “Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus.” And Christ was no weak, effeminate man; he was a strong, powerful, upright man.

Paul says it plainly: “Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.” That is how we are going to rise. If twelve of you have cars that run fine and a brother in the body can't even fix his car, and you shut your mouth and do nothing, you are weak. That is not how our black men are supposed to stand. Israelites are commanded to help each other.

So every school should have its mechanics, carpenters, plumbers and electricians helping the people in the body, making videos so the next brother can do it too. Instead of paying $1,900 you pay $300 for the parts, and brothers with the spirit fix the car. That's alms deeds; that's helping your nation.

We used to have that. Black people used to speak to each other in the street because we had a commonality, a common struggle. Now we have fallen apart. Bearing one another's burdens is how the nation is gathered together and becomes an economic force: that is the mind of Christ and the law of Christ.

precepts.text: Wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence.
precepts.point: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. Looking means acting when a brother struggles.

note.label: The Highway of the Upright: an Israelites's Strait Journey

precepts.why:
Looking on the things of others means building something together, and economics must be part of our mindset as we walk to build a nation. Solomon says: “For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it.”

Wisdom is a defence: generational wisdom passed down from father to son, grandfather to son. Esau has law in his house, and the grandfather passes the torch and teaches hard lessons that save heartache; that is why they had the head start, and why they are so relaxed at their jobs. We are behind in everything. Half of black folks have a credit score below 620, locked out of access to capital; before we wake up in the morning, half of us are in bondage.

Money is a defence. Walking the commandments, evil is going to come upon you: what happens when they take your job? So build businesses we can self-employ in, food distribution, brothers helping each other. Teach your children about secured loans and secured credit cards and the three credit bureaus, Experian, TransUnion and Equifax. And a single, divorced brother paying out his money has less of a defence than a man married in proper order.

“wisdom giveth life to them that have it”, and to have it you have to be taught it. That is why they try to stop us from teaching that we are the twelve tribes of Israel: scattered, we lost our nationality, heritage and commandments. The father in the house, with Christ at his head, is the one to break that cycle.

precepts.text: Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling, now much more in his absence; this goes into cleansing you from secret faults.
precepts.point: Who can understand his errors? Cleanse thou me from secret faults. This should be your reason to be in this walk, not to appear righteous, but because God shall bring every work into judgment; work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.” Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling, now much more in his absence, when nobody is watching.

This goes into cleansing you from secret faults. Your reason to be in this walk should not be to appear righteous, but because God shall bring every work into judgment.

precepts.text: Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling when the teacher is absent.
precepts.point: People will come, even family members, saying no one is coming to save you and you must save yourself with guns. You must stay steadfast and answer the Most High's cry with patience.

note.label: Isaiah 30: Woe to the Rebellious Children Who Trust in Egypt

precepts.why:
Blessed are all they that wait for him, and the waiting is your own work: “Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.”

Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling when the teacher is absent. When people come, even family members, saying no one is coming to save you and you must save yourself with guns, you must stay steadfast, holding patience through the trials and tribulations, obeying much more in his absence than in his presence, and answer the Most High’s cry with patience.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory. So you should not do anything through arguing and strife, nor through vainglory. Vainglory is you doing things to be seen by everyone, getting glory from man, which is vain. The glory that you get from men is vain, but you like that vainglory.

A lot of times you might go over a good lesson and it helps a lot of people, and people tell you, brother, that class really helped me, that was a great class. They appreciate it. But in them letting you know that, some brothers let that thing get to their head. I have seen it happen to many brothers, and you become full of yourself, and you start desiring it. You love that vainglory now. Instead of saying all praises to the Lord, you say, yeah, that was a good class I did, you do not know how many hours I sat down and put that thing together.

But in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves. It must be done in lowliness of mind, meaning you have got to humble yourself. Each of us has got to esteem others better than themselves. In order to do that you have got to see qualities in your brother and appreciate them. Why is he saying this? Because Christ taught it to them. Because in Matthew 18 they were asking who is going to be greater in the kingdom, and Christ had to correct them and teach them. Esteeming the person better than you is going to take away that ego. If you esteem the next person better than you, that spirit is not going to jump on you.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves. A lot of you run your household on strife and vainglory. You cannot run your household on ego.

Some of you do not teach your wives because you do not want her to know something you do not know, do not want her to study, because one day she may ask a question you cannot answer and your pride and ego take over. There was a brother whose wife could not do anything, could not leave the house without him, did not know how to drive; he was not pouring into her at all. If she is supposed to be that tower against death, how is she going to guide you with the scriptures when you are going through something if you never built the tower up? Instead of counseling with us about how you do not build your wife up, you come and say, my wife does not know anything. Were you studying with her? No.

Like when we go on these trips: sometimes the bishop, deacons, captains, or officers get sick, but we're out there doing the work. “For indeed he was sick nigh unto death: but God had mercy on him”. God had mercy because he was doing the work.

points: “Receive him therefore in the Lord with all gladness; and hold such in reputation”. He put his life on the line to serve them, to help Paul get to these people and build them up. He almost died from sickness doing the work. “Because for the work of Christ he was nigh unto death”. All of us in the nation of Israel should have that mindset to do Christ's work, even when it comes down to sickness. We still have to get the work done.

“not regarding his life, to supply your lack of service toward me.” He didn't regard his own life in doing what Paul asked. To hell with it, I'm still going. I'm not feeling a hundred; I'm still going.
